line.title: Tribunal Rotae Romanae
line.courtDescription: The Tribunal Rotae Romanae sits in {venue}. {gallery} Archmagistrate {judge} presides. The court assigns {interpreter} to render the bench's Latin.

venues: the Hall of the Rota, under a fresco of the Last Judgement
a vaulted chamber of the Apostolic Palace, lit by a single window
a cold courtroom of grey marble, with the Empire's keys carved over the bench
the chapter house of a cathedral, cleared of its pews for the hearing
gallery: Clerics in black fill the benches and do not whisper.
A row of notaries writes down every word in three copies.
The gallery is empty: the Rota does not sit for an audience.
Two Swiss halberdiers stand at the door and look at nothing.

la: Nulla accusatio in tabula scripta est. Tribunal non sedet. Discede.
tr: There is no charge written on the sheet. The court does not sit. You may go.

la: Tribunal Rotae Romanae sedet. Adstat reus {name}. Audiatur et altera pars, sed lex non flectitur.
In nomine Imperii Sancti, causa {name} aperitur. Iustitia aequa est, sed non mitis.
Sedet Rota. Reus {name}, attende: hic nihil fortuna, omnia lex.
tr: The Tribunal of the Roman Rota is in session. The accused, {name}, stands before it. The other side shall be heard, but the law does not bend.
In the name of the Holy Empire, the case of {name} is opened. Justice here is fair, but it is not gentle.
The Rota sits. Accused {name}, listen: nothing here is left to chance, everything to the law.

la: Advocatus non admittitur. Interpres tibi datus est; nihil aliud.
Nemo pro te loquetur. Interpres verba mea reddet, et tua.
tr: No advocate is admitted. You have been given an interpreter, and nothing more.
Nobody will speak for you. The interpreter will render my words, and yours.

la: Accusaris de crimine: {charge}. Poena in tabula: {amount}.
Scriptum est in tabula: {charge}. Pretium: {amount}.
tr: You are accused of: {charge}. The penalty on the sheet: {amount}.
It is written on the sheet: {charge}. Its price: {amount}.

la: Quid respondes? Confiteris, an negas?
tr: What do you answer? Do you confess, or do you deny?

la: Misericordia non est in hoc foro. Responde ad accusationem.
Misericordiam a Deo pete, non a Rota. Confiteris, an negas?
tr: There is no mercy in this court. Answer the charge.
Ask God for mercy, not the Rota. Do you confess, or do you deny?

la: Confessio accepta est. Poena uno gradu minuitur, nec amplius.
tr: The confession is accepted. The sentence is lowered by one step on the tariff, and no further.

la: Quod es, non quod fecisti, in tabula scriptum est. De hoc non disputatur.
tr: What is written on the sheet is what you are, not what you did. That is not open to argument.

la: Interpres tibi dicet quanta sit spes defensionis tuae. Nihil celatur.
tr: The court states the odds plainly, so nobody can call it unfair: your defence carries {chance} in a hundred. If it fails, the denial is perjury, and the sentence rises one step.

la: Loquere. Rota audit.
tr: Speak. The Rota is listening.

la: Accusatio non probata est. Absolvo te. Tabula deletur.
Defensio valet. Absolutus es; discede in pace.
tr: The charge is not proven. I acquit you. The sheet is struck out.
The defence holds. You are acquitted; go in peace.

la: Negasti quod verum est. Periurium addis crimini tuo.
Defensio cecidit, et mendacium tuum cum ea. Poena augetur.
tr: You denied what is true. You add perjury to your crime.
The defence has fallen, and your lie with it. The sentence is raised.

la: Reus est. Condemno.
Probatum est. Condemno te secundum legem.
tr: Guilty. I condemn you.
It is proven. I condemn you according to the law.

la: Poenam tibi irrogo secundum tariffam Imperii.
tr: I pass sentence according to the Empire's tariff: {sentence}.

la: Bona tua publicantur, usque ad summam poenae.
tr: Your goods are confiscated, up to the full sum of the penalty: {amount}.

release: The cell door opens. A cleric reads the release aloud in Latin, then once more for you. The Rota does not see you out.
Sententia expleta est. Your sentence is served. The guards return what little the court left you.
The interpreter waits at the gate: "The Rota considers the matter closed. It also remembers it."
